content: I'll start by reading the test image to identify the affected plant part and key visual features.
The test image shows two banana pods (fruits) with dark black irregular lesions on yellow skin — the affected part is clearly the **pod**. Now let me read the part index to narrow candidates.

The part index confirms pod-affecting candidates from the possible classes are: **Anthracnose** and **Cigar_End_Rot**. I must view 4 references across 4 different classes. Let me start with the Anthracnose pod reference.
The Anthracnose pod shows brownish irregular patches rather than stark black lesions. Let me now check Cigar_End_Rot.
Cigar_End_Rot shows dark tips on green unripe bananas — very different from the test image's yellow fruits with widespread black spots. I need 2 more class views to fulfill the 4-class requirement.
Cordana Leaf Spot shows brown spots with yellow halos on green leaves — clearly a leaf disease, not matching the test image. One more class view needed.

Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka shows yellow/dark streaks on banana leaves — clearly a leaf disease unrelated to the test image.

**Analysis Summary:**

- **Test image**: Two ripe/yellow banana pods with large, irregular stark black lesions/spots distributed across the fruit surface; the bottom pod shows extensive coalescing dark rot.
- **Part**: Pod (fruit)
- **Part index candidates**: Only **Anthracnose** and **Cigar_End_Rot** affect pods in this dataset.
- **Cigar_End_Rot**: Shows dark dry rot confined to the distal tip of green unripe bananas — completely different pattern.
- **Anthracnose**: Shows irregular dark lesions on banana pods; the test image's widespread black sunken spots on ripe yellow fruit are classic post-harvest Anthracnose (*Colletotrichum musae*), which causes expanding dark lesions on ripening fruit.
- **Leaf diseases** (Cordana_Leaf_Spot, Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka, Panama_Disease, Bunchy_Top): All affect leaves/whole plant, not matching the pod with black lesions.
